passages.text: Preface

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: The secondary curriculum has been revised in the light of National Education Policy 2010 which emphasises learning English as an international language for communicating locally and globally.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: The English For Today textbooks have been developed to help students attain competency in all four language skills, i.e. listening, speaking, reading and writing.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: The development of curriculum, syllabus and textbook is a continuous process.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: In continuation of it, this book has been developed and rationally evaluated by a group of experts, which included curriculum specialists, subject specialists, teacher trainers and classroom teachers.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: The contents and illustrations of this book have been developed in order to suit the learners age and cognitive level.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: The book emphasises practising language skills through a variety of meaningful and enjoyable activities.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: The publication of teacher's guide is under process.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: The teacher's guide will help teachers plan lessons more effectively and teach students communicatively through teaching learning activities.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: My heartfelt gratitude goes to the curriculum developers, writers, illustrators and coordinator who worked under tremendous time constraints.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: Without their sincerity, commitment and hard work, it would not have been possible for NCTB to develop the English textbook 'English For Today', making it available to teachers and students all over the country by January 2013.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: Recently, the national evaluation and tryout program has been completed to make correction and revision of the textbook.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: I hope the outcomes of the program will be reflected in this revised edition.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: Any constructive suggestions for the improvement of the textbook will be welcomed and incorporated in future editions.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: I also sincerely thank all involved in the production, revision and publication of this textbook.

passages.heading: Preface
passages.text: If this book is used properly, it will no doubt facilitate learning English at the desired level.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Lesson 1: Can you live alone?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: A

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Look at the pictures and discuss in pairs the following questions.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Can you live alone in a house?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Make a list of the problems you think you will have if you live alone in a house, e.g. having accidents, cooking, etc.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: B

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Read the story and answer the questions that follow

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Long ago, a young man who lived in a village ,found his life full of problems and sufferings.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Quarrels, ill-feelings, jealously, enmity - all were part of everyday life there.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So he left his house and went to a jungle to live by himself.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: There he made a nice little hut with wood , bamboo and reeds.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: "Ah, how happy I am here!"

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: said the man to himself.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: But one day he found some mice in his hut.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The little creatures soon made holes in his blanket.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So he brought a cat to kill the mice.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The cat needed milk.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So he brought a cow.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The cow needed grass and hay.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So he brought a cowboy.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The cowboy needed food.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So he took a wife to cook meals.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Then children were born to them, and the man found himself again in a family.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So nobody can live alone, unless that person is either angles or devils.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: People need food, shelter, companions and cooperation.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: They need to help each other.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: And if they live in a family or community, their need can be fulfilled.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Hence living in society can make people good and happy citizens.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: C

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Close your book and answer the question. What five things did the young man do in the jungle? Now divide into groups of five. Tell the story to the groups sequentially.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: D

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Answer these following questions. First discuss in pairs, then write the answers individually.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Why did the young man leave his house?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Where did he make a hut?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: What did he make the hut with?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Was the man happy in his hut?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: How did he find himself again in a family?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Where and how can a person be happy?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: What is the moral of the story?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: E

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Look at the pictures (a---j). Read the following texts (1---10). Match the pictures with the texts. Write the numbers of the texts next to a, b, c, etc. The first one is done for you.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: As people live in a community or society, they often have problems.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: A family may have a problem with a particular member (a son / daughter) who keeps bad company.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So, they discuss to solve the problem.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: To prevent theft or robberies, constant security measures are often necessary within the village / city area.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: A community may have a problem like they don't have a primary school in the village or locality.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So the people need to discuss the issue in a meeting and find out how to set up a school for their children.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Cooking should not be exclusively a woman's job.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Young learners must cultivate virtues and acquire knowledge and skills to prepare themselves to carry out their roles as good citizens.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So they need to study formally in the institutions.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: To establish peace and harmony among the people in a locality / village, often experienced, elderly people mediate between quarreling people.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Only studying at school is not enough for the young learners.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: They must also acquire knowledge and skills at home as well as from media, clubs, sports, libraries and so on.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: People in a society / locality, often need to buy things at home.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: So there are vendors selling necessary things.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: In a village or locality, roads often need repairing for easy movement of people and transport.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Along with acquiring knowledge and skills, the youths must cultivate good qualities like having genuine sympathy for the weak and the poor.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: They should help the needy, show respect to others and have a strong sense of dignity of work.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: F

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Discuss in pairs and write the answer to the following question:

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: What can we do at home and in the locality to become good citizens?

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: A

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Discuss in groups the possible answers to the following question. Then read the text in B and answer the questions.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: What else do you need in addition to food, shelter and company to become a good citizen?

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: B

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Read the text.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: To be a good citizen, you have to prepare yourself to do good work in society.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Well, then how can you prepare yourself?

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: First, you need knowledge.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Today's society is knowledge-based.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Without having modern sciences, technologies including ICT and other necessary subjects, you will have difficulty living a good life.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: The other areas you, as a good citizen, should have knowledge about are:

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: our country, its constitution, geography and people

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: our state, its executive and legislative powers

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: our judicial system

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: our government and its structures and functions

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: our history, cultures, traditions, literature, moral values and religions

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: our socio-economic activities and educational system

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Second, you need skills to do things.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Knowledge is not enough.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: You must be able to apply your knowledge to do things practically.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Finally, knowing and doing things will bring about a change in your behaviour towards others.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: This behavioral change will show your attitudes towards others, that is, it will show how you think and feel about a person or thing.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Let's take an example.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Suppose you, as a student, need to know about `group work' in the classroom.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: So you ask yourself or your teacher or anybody, "What is group work?"

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Or you may find about it in a book.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: In this way, you can know, or you may have the knowledge, about group work: To do group work. the class has to be divided into groups.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Each group is to do some tasks given by the teacher or in the textbook.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: The group members will discuss and share ideas and points, and finally one member will write the answer.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: All this is knowledge about group work.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Then you start working in groups.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: In each group you take turns discussing points, answering questions, etc.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: In this way you actually do the task.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Your teacher may monitor and help you to do the work.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Lastly, through regular group work it is expected that there will be noticeable changes in your behaviour.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Possible changes are:

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: You will develop the attitude of freely mixing and talking with your classmates and teacher.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Your shyness will gradually disappear.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: You will develop the attitude of helping and cooperating with each other.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: You will learn to behave in a democratic way.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Most importantly, these behavioral changes taking place in you inside the classroom will be carried over outside the classroom, in real-life situations.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: C.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: Suppose you have learned at school how to make your drinking water safe & when and how much you should drink it in a day. Now write what changes the knowledge and skills from this lesson can bring about in your behavior.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Knowledge, skills and attitudes
passages.text: D.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: What is responsibility?

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: A responsibility is a duty or an obligation TO DO something.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: For example, you have the responsibility to take care of your parents in their old age, to attend school and pursue your studies properly and so on.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: You have also the responsibility to society and the government, e.g. to help a neighbor in trouble or to cast your vote if you are 18 or over.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: A responsibility is also an obligation or a duty NOT TO DO something.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: For example, you have the responsibility not to steal a book from a public library or not to put your building materials on the footpath.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: These are your responsibilities as citizens.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: But there are responsibilities of the government as well.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: Our government has the responsibilities to provide for its citizens "the basic necessities of life, including food, clothing, shelter, education and medical care".

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: The government also has the responsibilities to protect the fundamental rights of its citizens to freedom of speech and expression, freedom of the press, freedom of religion, equality of all before law, etc.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: The knowledge, skills and attitudes you have gained at home, at school and in society will help you to accept your responsibilities and to carry them out effectively.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Responsibilities
passages.text: Remember, discharging your responsibilities will be good for you, good for your family and friends, and good for your society and country as a whole.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Suppose your kids are demanding the latest video game, your boss wants that report done today by five, and your partner wants to know what’s for dinner tonight.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Stress and anxiety are everywhere.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: In this situation, to keep fit as well as to give them the best you need to do something.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: And here comes yoga to help you.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Understanding yoga

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Yoga is a kind of posture and breathing exercises.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: It brings together physical and mental disciplines to achieve peace of body and mind, helping you relax and manage stress and anxiety.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Traditional yoga puts emphasis on behavior, diet and meditation.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: But if you’re just looking for better stress management –and not an entire lifestyle change , yoga can still help.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Yoga trainers gradually choose easier to complex activities for participation.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: However, all practitioners do not necessarily need the same kinds of practice.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: The health benefits of yoga

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: The potential health benefits of yoga are numerous and may include.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Stress reduction

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: With its quiet, precise movement, yoga draws you focus away from you busy, chaotic day and towards calm as you move your body through poses that require balance and concentration.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Increased fitness.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: As you learn and refined new poses , you may enjoy improved balanced, flexibility , rang of motion and strength.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: And this means you're less likely to injure yourself in other physical endeavors or in your daily activities.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Management of chronic health condition.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Yoga might help with a variety of health condition, such as cancer, depression, pain, anxiety and insomnia, fatigue and mood.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Yoga can also help reduce heart rate, and blood pressure .

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Weight loss.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: If you're over weight or have eating disorder, yoga may help you make the healthy lifestyle changes necessary to change control of your eating and drop those extra pounds.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: While you should not expect yoga to cure you are offer you relief 100 percent, it can help some health conditions when combined with standard treatment.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: And if you already enjoy good health, yoga can be an enjoyable supplement to your regular fitness routine.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: With the curtains closing on the 2012 London Olympics, it's impossible not to look back and reflect on the greatest performances by Olympic athletes.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: [Photo: Kirby Lee. USA TODAY Sports]

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: The Olympics have many memorable moments and athletes we'll remember by name alone.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: The list is quite big.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Michael Phelps and Usain Bolt are the latest addition to this list of the bests.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: They make London Olympics stand apart.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: If there is any question like this: "What is the standout performance of London 2012?

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: , perhaps the answer is " The London Games gave us Michael Phelps vs.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: The first one

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: is an already decorated Olympian, who puts the finishing touches on his great athletic careers And another comes up with a new definition of fast.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Two of the most popular Olympic sports, sprinting and swimming, saw their two biggest stars and captivated ,audiences.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: They'd also dominated the 2008 Beijing Games, but Phelps and Bolt cemented their legacies in London.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Phelps, the American swimmer, passed gymnast Larissa Latyniafor the most Olympic medals ever.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Bolt was the third man to repeat as a 100-meter gold medalist and the first as a 200-meter gold medalist, and he broke his own Olympic record by running the 100 in 9.63 seconds.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Once Phelps and Bolt were back in their pool and track, the story lines changed.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Phelps is the most-decorated Olympian ever, with 22 overall medals: 18 gold, two silver, two bronze.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Bolt is the most accomplished Olympic sprinter, with the unprecedented double, making clear that he's the fastest man in the world.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: But there's a debate: Who had the better Olympics?

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: It'd be tough to top Phelps' eight gold medals in Beijing, but what if we're only talking London?

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: London was Phelps' grand finale.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: He won four gold’s and two silvers in seven events, and he says he'll never race again.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: London was Bolt's chance to prove he's still the greatest.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Bolt wins six gold medals in six Olympic finals.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: He is the first man ever in the history of the modern Games to sweep the 100 and 200 in back-to-back Olympics.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Not to mention the addition of back-to-back relay gold’s.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: And Bolt became a legend, in his own words.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Phelps already was.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Bolt is just 25 years old, so there is no telling how long he can be on top of the sprinting world.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: What if he decides to "retire" from sprinting to focus on the 400 meters, just to break another world record or two?

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: It would be amazing- and entirely plausible for him to accomplish.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Who had the better 2012 Games?

passages.text: Childhood outdoor pastimes 'in decline'

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Traditional childhood pastimes of climbing trees and playing conkers are in decline, according to survey by the RSPB (Royal Society for the Protection of Birds).

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: It's a charitable organization registered in England and Wales.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: The survey shows that people under 34 recall far fewer such childhood outdoor experiences than their counterparts over 55, according to a survey by RSPB.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: People were asked which of 12 Childhood outdoor experiences they could remember.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: The answer included making dens, daisy chains, climbing trees, playing conkers and feeding birds.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Four out of five boys climbed trees and the same number of girls made daisy chains.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: But the survey showed the numbers declining among the newer generations.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Some 15% more of those aged over 55 had these outdoor experiences in their childhood, compared with those between 15-34 years old.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Some 92% of the public agreed that experiences of nature were still important to children, and agreed that schools should play a role in providing them to all children.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: The survey has highlighted the positive impact of contact with nature on a child's education, health, well-being and social skills.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: At the same time, there has been a decline in these opportunities, with negative consequences for children, families and society - a condition now known as nature deficit disorder.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: Mike Clarke, chief executive of the RSPB, will meet parliament members on Tuesday to urge the government to join other organizations in providing children with first-hand experiences of the natural environment. ...

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: "We believe this guidance should include the many positive impacts to children of having contact with nature and learning outside the classroom."

passages.text: A recent survey shows that during the last twenty years, teenagers have gone through significant changes in choosing their pastimes.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?
passages.text: The survey results are presented through a graph, which shows that there is a steady rise in young people's tendency to watch TV.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Have you any favourite pastime?

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: May Day or International Workers Day is observed on May 1 all over the world today to commemorate the historical struggle and sacrifices of the working people to establish an eight-hour workday.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: It is a public holiday in almost all the countries of the world.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Since the Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries in Europe and the US, the workers in mills and factories had been working a long shift, fourteen or even more hours a day.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: On May 1st in 1886, inspired by the trade unions. half of the workers at the McCormic Harvester Company in Chicago went on strike demanding an eight-hour workday.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Two days later, a workers' rally was held near the McCormic Hervester Company and about 6000 workers had joined it.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The rally was addressed by the labour leaders.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: They urged the workers to stand together, to go on with their struggle and not to give in to their bosses.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Just at this moment some strikebreakers started leaving the meeting place.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The strikers went down the street to bring them back.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Suddenly about 200 policemen attacked them with clubs and revolvers.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: One strike was killed instantly, five or six others were seriously wounded and many of them were badly injured.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The events of May 1, 1886 is a reminder that workers will continue to be exploited until they stand up and speak out to gain better working conditions, better pay and better lives.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Industrial Revolution: the period, especially in the 18th and 19th centuries Europe, when machines were invented and first factories were established.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: Trade Union: an organization that represents workers of mills and factories.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: 21 February is a memorable day in our national history.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: We observe the day every year as International Mother Language Day.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The day is a national holiday.On this day, we pay tribute to the martyrs who laid down their lives to establish Bangla as a state language in undivided Pakistan in 1952.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: This is known as the Language Movement.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The seed of the Language Movement was sown on 21 March 1948 when Mohammad Ali Zinnah, the then Governor General of Pakistan, at a public meeting in Dhaka declared that Urdu would be the only official language of Pakistan.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The declaration raised a storm of protest in the eastern part of the country.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The protest continued nonstop, gathering momentum day by day.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: It turned into a movement and reached its climax in 1952.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The government outlawed all sorts of public meetings and rallies spot it.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: The students of Dhaka University defied the law and they brought out a peaceful protest procession on 21 February 1952.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: When the procession reached near Dhaka Medical College, the police opened fire on the students, killing Salam, Rafiq, Barkat and Jabbar.

passages.heading: Learning outcomes
passages.text: This kindled the sparks of independence movement of Bangladesh.

passages.heading: Lesson 4 : International Mother Language Day – 2
passages.text: 21 February has been observed as Shaheed Diboshevery year throughout the country in remembrance of the martyrs of language movement of 1952.

passages.heading: Lesson 4 : International Mother Language Day – 2
passages.text: The occasion begins at the early hours of the day with mourning songs that recall the supreme sacrifices of our language martyrs.

passages.heading: Lesson 4 : International Mother Language Day – 2
passages.text: People wear black badges and go to the Shaheed Minarbarefoot in procession, singing mourning songs.

passages.heading: Lesson 4 : International Mother Language Day – 2
passages.text: They place wreaths at the Minar.

passages.heading: Lesson 4 : International Mother Language Day – 2
passages.text: Many of them visit the graves of the martyrs at Azimpur graveyard and pray for them.

passages.heading: Lesson 4 : International Mother Language Day – 2
passages.text: They also attend various programmes organized in remembrance of the language martyrs.

passages.heading: Lesson 4 : International Mother Language Day – 2
passages.text: The UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) on 17 November in 1999 proclaimed February 21 as the International Mother Language Day in recognition of the sacrifices of the martyrs for the rightful place of Bangla.

passages.heading: Lesson 4 : International Mother Language Day – 2
passages.text: The day is now annually observed worldwide to promote awareness of linguistic and cultural diversity and multilingualism.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: 'Pahela Boishakh' is the first day of Bangla new year.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: The day is a public holiday.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: This day has a special significance for us as it forms a part of Bangalee culture and tradition.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: People from all walks of life, irrespective of their ethnic identity or religious beliefs celebrate the day with traditional festivities.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: On this day, the whole of Bangladesh is in a festive mood.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: The day inspires people to start life with renewed hopes and inspirations.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: Every year the day is celebrated traditionally.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: People wake up early in the morning have a bath and wear their traditional clothes.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: Women wear white saris with red borders and adorn themselves with colourful churis and flowers, while men dress , themselves with pajamas and punjabis.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: It is a day when people love eating traditional food.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: The most colourful event of the day is held in Dhaka.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: Early in the morning, people in hundreds and thousands pour in from all directions to attend the cultural function a Ramna Batamul organized by Chhyanata.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: The cultural programme begins just with sunrise and the renowned artists of the country take part in the programme that start with the famous Tagore-song Esho-he-Boishakh, Esho Esho ........ .

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: Artists also sing traditional folk songs, and display classical dances with the rhythm of musical instruments.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: People also come to join the colourful processions, the biggest carnival of the country organized by the Fine Arts students of Dhaka University.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: The procession usually displays the traditional practices of Bangalee culture.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: The masks and wreaths won by the people are so fascinating!

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: Often they symbolize contemporary worries or happiness in the national life.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: It attracts an increasing number of foreign tourists every year.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: The day is also observed all over the country.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: Different social and cultural organizations and educational institutions celebrate the day with their own cultural programmes.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: On this day, newspapers bring out special supplements.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: There are also special programmes on the radio and television.

passages.heading: Lesson 6: Pahela Boishakh
passages.text: The celebration of Pahela Boishakh marks a day of cultural unity for the whole nation irrespective of caste and creed.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: One group leader says, “The scarcity of food will be a serious problem.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: It is true that our agriculturists have developed new varieties of rice and its per acre production has definitely increased.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: But the rate of increase in food production cannot keep pace with the rate of population growth.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: This is because our land is fixed. i.e. we cannot increase it, while our population is increasing rapidly."

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: Another group leader comes up with the housing problem in the country, which he says adds much to the food problem.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: He continues, "Families are growing larger in size and breaking into smaller families.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: Each such family needs a separate house to live in.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: Also the arable fields are being divided by these smaller families among themselves.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: Mills and factories are being set up, which occupy a considerable portion of our land.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: So when we need more land to grow more food to feed more mouths, our land is shrinking day by day.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: If our population grows at the present rate, a day will come when many people will not find any land to build a house on.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: And, as a result, many of them might live on trees or on the floating boats in the rivers."

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: “No way,” another student argues.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Our food and shelter
passages.text: Thank you students," Ms Choudhury says, "You're quite right.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: The Year before last, Lipi, a 14-year old girl was in class 9 in a rural school in Rangpur.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: Lipi is the eldest of five children---three daughters and two sons.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: Their father is a day labourer working on other people's land and mother is a homemaker and a part-time worker at other people's houses.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: The parents, particularly the mother, found it real difficult to raise five children on the small income the father could earn.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: Perhaps that is why Lipi's father wanted to marry her off.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: But Lipi was not ready to accept What her parents wanted to impose on her.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: She wanted to pursue her education.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: So long her mother stood by her, though secretly.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: But when her father arranged her marriage with Tara Mia, the only son of a farmer in the same village, she became a little upset.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: Tara Mia was a widower-illiterate, but well off.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: His father had a few acres of arable land and was influential in the village.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: The story of Lipi
passages.text: The marriage seemed to be inevitable.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: Read what Ms Choudhury talks with her students about learning English.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: Today there are many jobs where you need English.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: This is because the world has become smaller.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: Vast distances are shortened by speedy transport.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: We can talk to a thousands of kilometres away on the phone or the Internet.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: So we can communicate with the whole world easily.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: English has made this communication easier.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: There are many countries in the world with many languages, but to communicate with you cannot speak all the languages.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: So you need a common language that you can use with more or less all the people in the world.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: English is that common language.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: You can talk to a Chinese toy maker, a French artist, an Arab ambassador or K Korean builder in one language -English.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: English for us in Bangladesh is all the more important.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: As we have seen earlier, we are too many people in a small country.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: So if you learn English, you have the best opportunity to find a good job, both within and outside the country.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: And that is good news for millions of our unemployed youths."

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: "But Miss, we learn English for 12 or 14 years, yet we do not find good jobs, " says Rumi.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: She then tells the class about what happened to her brother.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: "This is a very important question, Rumi.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: We should learn how to use English both orally and in writing for doing things as needed in our work, such as communicating with others at personal, social, national and international levels.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: But unfortunately, at the moment we are learning English mainly for our exams," continues Miss Choudhury.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: "Remember, English can greatly help you become skilled workforce."

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: Side by side with your textbook, the radio, television, newspapers, magazines, computers and other supplementary materials will greatly help you.

passages.heading: Lesson 5: Let's become skilled workforce
passages.text: And during our classroom activities, we'll see how we can learn this English."

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: Meherjan lives in a slum on the Sirajgonj Town Protection Embankment.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: Her polythene-roofed shelter looks like a cage.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: She is nearly 45 but looks more than age.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: In front of her shelter, she is trying to make a fire to cook the day's only meal.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: Her weak hands, day's only meal.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: Her weak hands tremble as she adds some fallen leaves and straw to the fire.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: The whispering wind from the river Jamuna makes the fire unsteady.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: The dancing of the flames reminds Meherjan of the turmoil in her life.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: Not long ago Meherjan had everything--- a family, cultivable land and cattle.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: The erosion of the Jamuna consumed all her landed property gradually.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: It finally claimed her only shelter during the last monsoon.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: It took the river only a day to demolish Meher's house, trees, vegetable garden and the bamboo bush.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: She had a happy family once.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: Over the years, she lost her husband and her family to diseases that cruel Hunger and poverty brought to the family.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: Now, she is the only one left to live on with the loss and the pain.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: The greedy Jamuna has shattered her dreams and happiness.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: There are thousand others waiting to share the same fate like Meherjan.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: Bangladesh is a land of rivers that affect its people.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: Erosion is a harsh reality for the people living along the river banks.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: During each monsoon many more villages are threatened by the roaring of rivers like the Jamuna the Padma and the Meghna.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: It is estimated that river, erosion makes at least 100,000 people homeless every year in Bangladesh.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: In fact, river erosion is one of the main dangers caused by climate change.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: The greed of the roaring rivers
passages.text: If we can't take prompt actions to adapt to climate change, there will be thousands of more Meherjans in our towns and villages every year.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Now read the following passage to know more about environmental pollution in Bangladesh.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Bangladesh is now apparently in the grip of all sorts of pollution like air pollution, soil Pollution and water pollution.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: The dwellers of the urban areas are the worst suffers of such pollution.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: The indiscriminate industrialization process in Bangladesh over the past decades has created significant environmental problems.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: We will now read about some of the most common types of environmental pollutions and ways of coping with them.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Air pollution

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Air pollution comes from a wide variety of sources.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: In Bangladesh poisonous exhaust industrial plants, brick kilns, old or poorly-serviced vehicles and dust from roads and construction sites are some of the major sources of air pollution.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: we can minimise this type of pollution by making less use of motor vehicles and avoiding the use of vehicles older than 20 years.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: We may also use proper lubricants to lessen the level of emission and pollutants.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: We can encourage people to use Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) or Liquid Petroleum Gas (LPG) for fuelling their cars .The government may relocate hazardous industries like brick kilns to areas away human habitations.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Water pollution

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Water pollution can occur in oceans, rivers, lakes, ponds and underground reservoirs.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: As different water sources flow together, the pollution can spread easily and quickly.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Causes of water pollution include:

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: increased sediment from soil

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: erosion

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: improper waste disposal and littering

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: leakage of soil pollution into water supplies

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: organic materials that decay in water supplies etc.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: In fact, polluting the land means polluting the water.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Throwing away a toxic substance on the ground near a water space means it eventually reaches a body of water.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: As a result, the water is polluted.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Industrial wastes must not be disposed in rivers or lakes.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: We need to be more careful about disposing household wastes too.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Use of pesticides means that when it rains on the lawn or garden, chemicals wash into the water bodies.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Therefore, we must be aware of the dangers of using pesticides as they may pollute our rivers, canals and lakes.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Soil pollution

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Among the most significant causes of soil pollution is the enormous volume of industrial waste which is being produced every day but not disposed properly.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: The mismanagement of household wastes, particularly the polythene shopping bags, has caused serious threat to the soil, and the drainage system.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Another cause for soil pollution is the use of agricultural pesticides, fertilizers etc.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Sometimes fuel leakages from automobiles may get washed away by rain and seep into the nearby soil.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Pesticides and fertilizers are useful for plant growth but their overuse has led to soil pollution.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Natural fertilizers and compost can be used instead of their chemical alternatives.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Recycling is another way to reduce and control soil pollution.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Recycling papers, plastics and other materials reduces the volume of refuse in landfills.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: De- forestation also causes erosion, pollution and the loss of fertility in the topsoil.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Environmental pollution
passages.text: Planting trees and re-forestation help prevent soil erosion and pollution.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Humans can neither change the sun's radiation nor the earth's orbit around the sun.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: But they can control the increase in the amount of greenhouse gases and its effect on the atmosphere.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Only during the last hundred years the carbon dioxide concentration has been raised alarmingly in the atmosphere and we humans car be held responsible for this.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: The main cause of the increase in carbon dioxide level in the atmosphere is the burning of fossil fuels.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Since the end of the 19th century, industrial activities increased rapidly giving rise to many factories.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: These factories required energy, which was produced through the combustion of coal.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Besides coal, other source of energy such as mineral oil and natural gas were also burned to heat our houses, move cars and airplanes or to produce electricity.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Nowadays, about 8 million barrels of crude oil are burned daily.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Every time a fossil raw material ' burned, it releases carbon dioxide into the air.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Therefore, it is clear that more and more greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide are being generated worldwide by humans.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Moreover, we are also strengthening the greenhouse effect by deforestation, which means cutting down trees.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Every year enormous areas of forests are destroyed by people to obtain wood and to clear regions for mining and to create pasture.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: This loss of the forest causes dual problems.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: Trees that are burned down release a large volumes of carbon dioxide gas into the air.

passages.heading: Lesson 3: Man and climate
passages.text: On the other hand, an important carbon dioxide storehouse is destroyed with the forests as forests absorb a lot of carbon dioxide from the air and deliver oxygen instead.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Read the text below and say if the statements that follow are true/false. If false, give the correct information.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Fish population is in serious danger from global warming.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Climate change is increasing the water temperature in rivers, lakes and seas.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: This means there is less food and oxygen available for fish.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: It also means the fish may not grow fully and may have fewer offspring.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Some fishes will become extinct if temperatures rise even by one or two degrees.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Climate change increases the pressure on fish population.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Fishes are one of the world's most valuable biological assets.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Forty percent of people in the world eat fish as their main source of protein.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: If we fail to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, we will increase the pressures on fish.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: As a result, people who depend on fish will suffer from hunger and poverty.

Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Some fishes cannot reproduce if the water is too warm.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: A two degree rise in temperature will make some species extinct.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Fishes are valuable economic investments.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!

passages.text: People will suffer a lot if greater pressure is put on fish.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Read the following text carefully to know about how we can save our environment.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: LET'S SAVE OUR PLANET!

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Everyone must play a part in protecting the environment.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: There are many things you can do on your own every day to help save the planet.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Here are some suggestions.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: REDUCE!

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Really, the best thing we can do for the planet is to use its resources properly.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Our consumer society is mainly responsible for the environmental crisis.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Here are some questions you can ask yourself before buying something, "Do I really need this?"

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: or "Is there another product which would do the same thing but more sustainable?"

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Or ask the question, "Will this last a long time?"

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Some other questions may be, "Do I know how this item was made, how it will be used and how it will be disposed of?”

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: REUSE!

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: What do you think of using your own ceramic cup or mug at your school or local club?

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: It means there are no plastic cups to throw away.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: You can wash it and reuse it every day.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Unfortunately, we are encouraged to buy a new "improved" item even if the one we have can be repaired or reused.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: When we buy things, we should buy items which are durable; we should use them properly, and have them repaired when necessary.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: If we practise this, many things can not only last a life-time, but also be passed on for future use.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: However, If something is truly unusable for its original purposes, try to be more creative and think of how else it might be used.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: When you're done with it, think of whether someone else might be able to use it.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: You can donate some of the things to the poor.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: You may also sell some of your used items through personal ads in a local newspaper.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: RECYCLE!

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Rather than throwing an item out when neither you nor anyone else can make use of it, have it recycled.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: And while recycling is not possible, it is better to send goods to a landfill or have them burned up.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Find out what types of materials can be recycled in your area.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Clean and sort the materials before putting them out in the bin.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Recycling your drink and food cans means there will be less trash in a resource recovery facility or landfill.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: Putting our fish in hot water!
passages.text: Moreover, a company can use the old cans to make new ones.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: A

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Read the following passage on Nepal.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: a.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Known as the Land of Everest, Nepal is one of the most charming countries in Asia.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: It is also known as the only Hindu Kingdom in the world.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: The Kingdom of Nepal is a small land of sublime beauty. 1t has some of the world's best and very important temples.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: It is a country that is rich in scenic beauty and cultural treasures.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: b.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Nepal lies between India and the Tibetan part of China.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: This small country has an area of 147,181 square kilometers.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Southern Nepal is tropical lowland known as the Tarai Plain.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: This part of Nepal has hot summers and warm winters.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Here temperatures reach up to 40°C in April and May and monsoon rains drench this region from June to September.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: The central hill-lands including the kathmandu and Pokhara valleys have a temperate climate and are also influenced by the monsoon.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: North of that is the slope of the main section of the Himalayan range.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: This part of Nepal has some of the highest peaks of the world including Everest.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: c .

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Nepal is home to nearly 29,000,000 people.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: The population is primarily rural.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Kathmandu, the capital city, has less than one million inhabitants.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Nepal`s demographic features are complicated not only by dozens of ethnic groups, but by different castes.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: In total, there are 103 castes and ethnic groups living in this small country.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: The two largest of such groups are known as Chetri and Bahun.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Others include Magar, Tharu and Tamang, Newar, Muslim, Gurung and Damai.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: About 48 percent of the people speak Nepali.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Among other language spoken are Maithali, Bhojpuri, Tharu and Tamang.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: d.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Nepal is the holy land of Lord Pashupatinath and Gautam Buddha where the Hindus and Buddhists have lived together in harmony for centuries.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: The Temple of Pashupatinath is the most sacred Hindu shrine and one of the four most important cities in the world for Shiva worshippers.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Lord Buddha, the light of Asia, was born in Lumbini in Nepal's southern plains, which makes this a sacred pilgrimage destination for the Buddhists as well.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: In fact, many Nepalese combine Hindu and Buddhist practices; many temples and shrines are shared between the two faiths, and some deities are worshipped by both Hindus and Buddhists.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: e.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: The Kathmandu Valley is the rich cultural heritage centre of Nepal.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: The three ancient cities of the Valley- Patan, Kathmandu and Bhaktapur- represent an epitome of harmony in urban design, elegant architecture and refined culture.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: These cities are famous for religious monuments unequalled in the world.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: The seven monument zones situated within the Valley have been named as World Heritage Sites by UNESCO.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: f.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Many festivals add dazzling colour to Nepal's vibrant culture, which are celebrated throughout the year.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Dasain or dusherra is celebrated nationwide in October.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: This is the most important of all Nepalese celebration and includes the biggest animal sacrifice of the year.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Tihar is celebrated in November.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Other festivals include the Holi and Chaitra Daisan.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Nepal, the land of Everest
passages.text: Some Hindu festivals are the Harihodhini Ekadashi, Maha Sivaratri and the Krishna Jayanti.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: When someone comes to Sri Lanka, they may often hear the word Ayubowan.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: This word means `May you have the gift of long life'.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: It is with this traditional greeting that everyone is welcomed to Sri Lanka.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Sri Lanka has many nicknames: Serendip, Ceylon, Tear drop of India, Pearl of the Indian Ocean, etc.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: These names reveal the richness and beauty of this island nation.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Many travelers, from ancient mariners and merchants to modern astronauts, have been attracted by the beauty of this island.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Sri Lanka is located in the Indian Ocean, just off the south-eastern coast of India.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Shaped like a teardrop, the island of Sri Lanka measures about 415 kilometers from north to south, and about 220 kilometres from east to west, with a total land area of about 65,600 square kilometres.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: It has more than 1340 kilometres of coastline.

passages.text: Despite its modest size Sri Lanka has a population of about 20 million.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Sri Lanka's economy has traditionally been based on agriculture.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: The emphasis is on exporting crops such as tea, rubber, and coconuts.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: In fact, Sri Lanka is the largest tea exporter of the world.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: The country is also a major producer and supplier of a variety of spices such as cinnamon, cardamom, pepper, cloves, and nutmeg.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Cinnamon first originated in Sri Lanka and was introduced later to the world by the Arab merchants.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: e.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Sri Lanka's archaeological treasures reflect the civilizations of the past that covered the golden age of Greece, the Roman Empire, Mayan citadels, and Napoleonic greatness.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: The culture that followed those glorious pasts has been enriched by the more recent influences of Western colonizers and Eastern traders.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: That resulted in developing a unique mix of races and religions, arts and crafts, festivals and costumes available in this small country.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: f.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Besides these man-made riches, one may find the God-given blessings of nature in Sri Lanka.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: The island is blessed with azure seas, sandy beaches, green hills, cascading waterfalls, abundant wildlife and a variety of flowers and fruits.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: The country abounds with coconut groves, spice gardens, tea estates and many other gardens and woods.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Travelers from all over the world come to Sri Lanka.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Here, a weary traveler can pass a gloriously lazy day by a palm-shaded lagoon looking at the endless ocean.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: And for the adventurous, days can be full of excitement, snorkeling, swimming, fishing or sailing.

passages.text: Anuradhapura

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Anuradhapura is one of the ancient capitals of Sri Lanka.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: The olden city is today surrounded by monasteries, covering an area of over sixteen square miles.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: The city is also significant in Hindu legend as the capital of King Ravana.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Bundala National Park

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Bundala National Park is one of Sri Lanka's leading destinations for birdwatchers.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: The park is also home to large populations of elephants, crocodiles, turtles and leopards.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Hikkaduwa is a little town on the south coast of SriLanka.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: It is well-known for its beach and corals.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: It is principally a tourist destination, and serves as a great beach with options to surf, snorkel and enjoy the sun.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Dambulla

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: Major attractions of this city include the biggest and greatest potted cave temple complex of Sri Lanka.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
passages.text: It is also famous for the Rangiri Dambulla Global Stadium, which was built in just 167 days.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Sri Lanka: The pearl of the Indian Ocean
