passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: Read the following text.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: Eid is the main religious festival of the Muslims in Bangladesh.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: Eid means happiness.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: Everyone wants to share this happiness with their near and dear ones.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: So most of the people, who are living outside their homes for different reasons have a strong desire to get back home during the Eid vacations.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: As a result, there is a mad rush in the buses, trains, or launches for the home-bound people.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: This often causes transport accidents that take away many lives.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: However, it cannot stop people's desire to meet their family, in-laws, or friends.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: What makes people rush for their homes in spite of serious hazards?

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: This is the pull of the roots.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: Do human beings have roots like the trees?

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: The answer is `yes' but unlike the roots of the trees they are invisible, they lie in our minds.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: It's these roots that make a bond between us and family members, in-laws, friends, neighbours or even between us and the land where we were born and grew up.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: In that sense our families, land of birth, relatives, our culture, traditions, or surroundings are our roots.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: And whereever we stay, we have a continuous pull of our roots.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: It's our roots that develop our identity making us what we are.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: When we lose that bond, we become rootless.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: Human beings who do not have any roots or contexts, are a non-entity.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: In other words, they do not have their own identity.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: Such persons are devoid of values, humanity, and social responsibilities.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: They don't know where they are from, and/or where they are heading towards.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: My roots
passages.text: This often makes them feel empty and lost.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Mainul Islam is a qualified farmer in Naogaon.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Mr Islam was very brilliant as a student.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He took his higher education from Bangladesh Agricultural University in Mymensingh.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: After completing his higher education, Mainul came back home and started advanced farming.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He has two other brothers who are graduates in different areas.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: The specialty of the Islam family is that they all are living in their village and all have fame in their own fields.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: His younger brother, who is a Rajshahi University graduate, is a science teacher in a local school.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: His youngest brother is a- social science graduate and he too would like to start a local NGO to work for this area.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: When asked "What makes you decide to stay here in this village?"

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: , Mr Islam smiled.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He said, "Look, it's true that we could leave this village for a city life.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: I could be an officer or my brother could be a bureaucrat.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: But it didn't attract us.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: We are sons of this soil.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Yes, we have education but does education prepare a person only to be an officer?

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Don't we have any obligation to the soil that has made us what we are?"

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He also added that every educated individual shouldn't be a job seeker.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He continued that since his discipline was Agriculture, after his education he took the occupation of a farmer.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: In response to the question whether they have any frustrations to live in a village, he confirmed that they were very pleased with their life.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He said, "I work in my own farm, stay with my family members, pass time with my old friends, and sleep at my own home.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: All these count a lot."

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Mr Islam is right.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Many people go to cities and forget or loosen their roots knowingly or unknowingly.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Mr Islam and his brothers are great - they never forgot their roots.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: They not only stuck to their own roots, they have been torch bearers for others to be respectful of their own roots.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Michael Madhusudan Dutt was a popular 19th-century Bengali poet and dramatist.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He was born in Sagordari on the bank of the Kopotaksho River, a village in Keshobpur Upazila under Jessore district.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: From an early age, Dutt aspired to be an Englishman in form and manner.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Though he was born in a sophisticated Hindu family, he took Christianity as a young man, much to the ire of his family, and adopted the first name Michael.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: In his childhood, he was recognized by his teachers as a precious child with a gift of literary talent.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: His early exposure to English education and European literature at home and his college inspired him to imitate the English in taste, manners and intellect.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Since his adolescence he started believing that he was born on the wrong side of the planet, and that his society was unable to appreciate his intellect.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He also believed that the West would be more receptive to his creative genius Michael was an ardent follower of the famous English poet Lord Byron.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: So after adopting Christianity, he went to Europe and started composing poetry and drama almost entirely in English.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: They showed his higher level of intellectual ability.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: However, he failed to gain the right appreciation.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: To his utter frustrations he found that he was not esteemed as a native writer of English literature.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Out of his frustration, he composed a sonnet in Bangla "Kopotaksha Nad", which earned him huge reputation in Bangla.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Gradually he could realize that his true identity lay in this Bengal and he was a sojourner in Europe.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: Afterwards he regretted his attraction for England and the west.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He came to Bengal and devoted himself to Bangla literature from this period.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: He is the poet to write the first Bangla epic Meghand Badh Kabya.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: My roots -2
passages.text: (Source: Wikipedia)

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: I understand your concern.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: Human flow from the rural areas to the urban areas is a big social problem in many countries like ours.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: These floating people are definitely a burden to the cities where they migrate.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: When the number is huge, it is difficult for any state to rehabilitate them quickly.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: See from the other side.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: The people you have referred to have lost their roots and they are unable to assimilate in the new culture.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: Maybe many of them are attracted by the gloss of the cities, but I'm sure it was a need to many others.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: People become rootless sometimes due to climate change, river erosion, social discrepancies, or poverty.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: However, you cannot solve this problem overnight.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: But you can take steps to improve their lifestyle.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: Why don't you form a committee with other young people in your locality that will teach them basic health, hygiene, and ethics?

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: It may better their life as well as help you minimize pollution.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: Give it a try.

passages.text: There might be different reasons for that.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: It may be due to government action, political decisions or to avoid conflict and warfare.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: Diaspora has come common consequences.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: Once people are away from their roots, they have a kind of cultural shocked.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: They take time to [dash] to the new culture.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: Sometimes never integrated.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: This [dash] them a feeling of home sickness.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: Due to economic or social realities in spite of their strong fascination for homeland or hometown diaspora people [dash] to get back to their roots.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: As a result, they have a kind of mental conflict and identity crisis which makes their life restless.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: Sometimes lack of social acceptance coupled with the economic inability, inadequate education, and loose family ties people [dash] involved in crimes.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: You may ask, “Does it [dash] that people won`t [dash] to other cities/countries”?.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: People will, as its 21st century when the world is a big global village.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: But we [dash] to be aware of the problems created from diaspora.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: It`s reality that people with better ties with their roots are less sufferer of this problem.

passages.heading: Lesson 4: In search of identity
passages.text: So instead of being allured by the ‘better life’ we can [dash] to be happy with what we have and gradually try to develop our condition without forgetting our roots.

passages.text: An e-mail is an electronic mail.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Media and models of e-communications
passages.text: It is a computer-aided way of exchanging digital text messages from a sender to one or multiple recipient/s.

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Media and models of e-communications

passages.heading: Lesson 1: Media and models of e-communications

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: The advantages of the Internet technology have made a good number of web sites to emerge to facilitate social relations among people around the world.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: These are known as social networking services or social networks.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: At present, Facebook is the most popular.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: Google+, Twitter, LinkedIn, etc. are other frequently used social services.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: Social network services are web-based and hence, provide ways for the users to interact through the Internet.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: These services make it possible to connect people sharing interests and activities across the borders and thus have made a lot for the users to feel that they really live in a global village.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: Why are social networks expanding so fast?

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: The answer is simple.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: Most of the social services are cost-free.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: You can make use of them free, paying a very little to your Internet service provider.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: Secondly, you can make your personal profile public before the entire online community.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: It is like presenting yourself before the entire world.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: You can also look into other people's profile if you are interested.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: It is simple and easy.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: Thirdly, social networks allow users to upload pictures, multimedia contents and modify the profile.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: Some services like Facebook allow users to update their profiles.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: Fourthly, networks allow users to post blog entries.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: User profiles have a section dedicated to comments from friends and other users.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: Finally, there are privacy protection measures too.

passages.heading: Lesson 2: Social network services
passages.text: A user himself or herself decides over the number of visitors/viewers, and what information should be shared with others.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: This time Rosamond was really disappointed as her mother wanted nothing.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: However, while they were passing by a chemist's shop, she saw some jars--blue, green, red, yellow and purple---and she seemed to have a fascination for a purple jar.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: But her mother answered as before, "Of what use would they be to me, Rosamond?"

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: Oh, Mamma, I would use it for a flower pot.'

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "But you have a flower pot and the jar you are dying for buying is not a flower pot."

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "Yet, Mamma, I like it so much ... !

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: " Then suddenly she cried, "Ouch!

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: A stone, mamma, a stone has got in my shoe.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: It hurts!"

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "Oh!

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: How did it get there?"

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "See, there's a hole in my shoe, Mamma.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: In fact, my shoes are quite worn out.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: Would you be so good as to buy me another pair?"

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "But, Rosamond, I haven't got money enough to buy shoes, jars, jewelry, buckles and all that you wish to buy."

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: Rosamond became sad again.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: Her mind flashed back to all those beautiful things she had seen that morning.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "But, Mamma, I like the purple jar very much.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: And now my foot hurts.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: Could you buy me only these two things --- the jar and a pair of shoes, please?"

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "No, Rosamond, you can buy only one thing.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: However, you may buy the other thing next month.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: And you have to decide which one you would like to buy now.'

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "I need the shoes badly," Rosamond began to argue with herself, but my heart is in that beautiful jar."

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: Then looking at her shoes, she told her mother, "These shoes are not so bad, except for the hole in one.

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: I think I can make them last till the end of the month, can't I?

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: Don't you think so, Mamma?"

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "I want you to think for yourself, dear."

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "Okay, if you please, I would like to have the purple jar.'

passages.heading: Lesson 7: The Purple Jar-2
passages.text: "Very well, you will have it."

passages.text: A

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: Read the last part of the story to see what happened to Rosamond's beautiful purple jar.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: Rosamond and her mother were going back to the chemist's shop.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: As they were walking, Rosamond had to stop once again to take another stone out of the broken shoe, and she often limped with pain.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: When they got back to the shop, Rosamond's mother asked her to carefully examine the jar before she bought it.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: But Rosamond was so excited that she bought it even without looking at what was inside the jar.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: Happily she came back home with her mother.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: Then Rosamond quickly brought some flowers from the garden and was going to put them into the jar.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: But as soon as she took the top off, she saw something dark inside, which gave off an unpleasant smell.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: "What is it, Mamma?

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: I didn't want this black thing and the terrible smell."

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: "Nor did I, my dear."

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: "But what shall I do with it?"

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: "That I can't tell."

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: "Okay, Mamma, I must pour it out and fill the jar with fresh water."

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: Then she made the jar empty.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: But to her great disappointment, she found that it was no longer a purple jar --- it was a plain white glass jar.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: With its coloured water gone, the jar did no longer look beautiful.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: Rosamond cried with tears of disappointment in her eyes.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: She was to cry more for her folly.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: Every day her shoes grew worse and worse, and she could neither run, dance, jump, nor go shopping with her mother.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: Thus Rosamond suffered for a whole month and learned a lesson the hard way.

passages.heading: Lesson 8: The Purple Jar-3
passages.text: She hoped that she would be wiser in future.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Once upon a time in Venice, there was a very rich merchant named Antonio.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: He many ships, that sailed in the sea.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: His ships carried different types of merchandise to other countries.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: He sold those goods in foreign countries.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: He bought spices and other valuables with the money and sold them in Venice.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Antonio was a good and kind man.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: He always helped the poor.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: The people of Venice loved him very much for his honesty and kindness.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Antonio had a close friend named Bassanio.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: He was a handsome young man and was born in a noble family.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Bassanio liked to live a very luxurious life.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: He loved grandeur and style.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: He spent more money than his earnings.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: As a result, he was very often short of money.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: In such situations, Bassanio would go to his best friend Antonio for help.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Antonio would, on the other hand, help him with cash.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: It so happened that Bassanio fell in love with a wealthy lady named Portia.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Portia was known not only for her beauty but also for her wisdom.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: She had softness towards Bassanio too.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: He wanted to visit Portia in a grand manner but he did not have any money.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: So he went to Antonio.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Bassanio said, " Dear friend Antonio, I am in great need of some money.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: I would like to visit Portia at Belmont, grandly dressed and with many servants.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: But I don't have any money right now.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Please help me to fulfill my intention."

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Antonio said, " This is not a problem, my friend.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: How much do you need?"

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: " Three thousand ducats (Venetian currency) will do."

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: " I don't have that much money with me now as all my ships have gone out in the sea with merchandise.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: But don't worry, my friend, I'll arrange three thousand ducats for you."

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: So he decided to borrow the sum from a moneylender named Shylock.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Shylock was a very crooked man.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Antonio and Shylock hated each other.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Shylock used to lend money with high interest.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: He would even send the debtor to prison if the latter failed to pay his debt.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: On the contrary, Antonio used to lend money to help those who needed it and would not charge any interest.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Shylock agreed to lend him money but on one condition.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: If he failed to repay the money in three months’ time, he would pay a penalty.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Shylock would cut a pound of flesh from any part of Antonio's body.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Antonio willingly agreed, thinking that his ships would soon return with all the rich merchandise and he could easily return the money to Shylock by selling them.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Shylock made Antonio sign a bond before giving him the money.

passages.heading: Lesson 9: A Pound of Flesh
passages.text: Antonio took the money and gave it to Bassanio.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Read the text and answer the following questions.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Bassanio went to Belmont to visit Portia grandly dressed, with many servants.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Portia's father had died lately.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Before his death he had thought of an unusual plan to find a good husband for his daughter.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: He wanted a man to marry Portia for herself and not for her wealth.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: He had three caskets made, one of gold, one of silver and one of lead.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: One of the caskets had Portia's portrait in it.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: The suitor who would first choose the casket with the portrait would marry her.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Many suitors went away when they heard about such a strange condition,

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: The first one to try was the prince of Morocco.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: He thought that silver and lead are poor metals.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: It is the casket made of precious metal that can hold the precious picture.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: So he chose the gold casket.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: But all he found was a picture of a skull with a message that said "All that glitters is not gold.."

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: The prince was very sad and went back home.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Then came the prince of Spain, He looked at the silver casket for a long time.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: On it was written, " He who chooses me will get what he deserves."

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: The prince had a very high opinion about himself'.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: He thought that he deserved the best.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: He therefore chose the silver casket and opened it.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Inside the, casket he found the picture of a blinking fool.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: He was very disappointed and offended.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: He immediately rode away.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Then it was Bassanio's turn.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: He looked at the caskets far a long time.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: He thought, "Appearances are often misleading.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Bad men appear good and they hide their inner ugliness under fine clothes," So He chose the pain looking lead casket.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: On opening the casket, he found the portrait of Portia inside.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Bassanio and Portia got married.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: There was great joy at Belmont and the newly married couple were spending their time happily.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: But Soon their happiness turned into sorrow by a piece of news.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: A messenger came with a letter from Antonio.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: The letter said, " Dear friend Bassanio, all my ships have been lost at sea. 1 cannot pay the money I owe to Shylock.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: So 1 have to pay the penalty.

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Dear friend, come and see me if possible. l would like to see you once before I die."

passages.heading: Lesson 10: The three caskets
passages.text: Bassanio quickly left for Venice.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Read the text; and answer the following questions.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: When Bassanio reached Venice, Antonio was already in the court of justice.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: They were waiting for the trial to begin.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The Duke entered the courtroom, took his sear and the trial began.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The Duke requested Shylock to be merciful and not to claim his pound of flesh.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: But Shylock would not listen to him.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Bassanio offered him twice the amount of money that Shylock lent Antonio but Shylock did not accept it.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: He said, " I claim my pound of flesh.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The law is on my side.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Antonio must pay the penalty written in the bond."

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The Duke was extremely sorry that he could do nothing to help Antonio.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The law was on Shylock's side and the law must be abided.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The Duke feared that though the wisest lawyer in Venice was coming to speak in defense of Antonio even he would not be able to save the merchant.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Soon a young clerk entered the courtroom with a letter from that lawyer.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The lawyer was ill and would not be able to come to the court.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: He requested the Duke to let his young friend, Doctor Balthazar, defend Antonio.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The Duke gave his permission, and Doctor Balthazar entered the courtroom.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: He looked very young, and the Duke doubted if the wisdom of the young lawyer could save Antonio.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: This young lawyer was no other than Portia in disguise and the young clerk was her friend; who was also in disguise.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Portia begged Shylock to be merciful and told him how God bestows mercy to those who are merciful themselves.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: " Mercy" Portia said, " brings a blessing to him who shows it and to him who receives it.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: All of us pray to God for mercy.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: But God will only have mercy on us if we have mercy on others."

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Shylock paid no heed to Portia.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: All he ,wanted was his pound of flesh.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Portia asked, "Can't Antonio pay the debt?"

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Bassanio cried, " Yes, he can pay it and even more. ...

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Even I can pay ten times the sum my friend borrowed from Shvlock."

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: " Won't you take the money.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Shy lock`'" Portia asked.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: " No, I demand the lawful penalty.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Give me my pound of flesh."

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: " Let me see the bond Shylock". said Portia.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Shylock handed the bond to her.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: She read it with great attention and then said. " you are right Shylock.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The law is on your side.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: You can claim the flesh.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: But I would request you one, more time to accept the sum Bassanio is offering you, and let me tear up the bond."

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: But Shylock would not give up his claim.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Portia then turned towards Antonio and said, " Get ready Antonio for Shylock to cut his pound of flesh.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: The law gives it to him."

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Shylock was filled with joy on hearing what Portia said.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: He began to praise Portia in disguise, for her wisdom and righteousness.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: He cried out, "Oh noble judge!

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Oh excellent young man, you are a second Daniel, who has come to this earth."

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Portia urged Shylock to cut the pound of flesh he demanded.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Delighted, Shylock walked towards Antonio with a knife in hand.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: He told Antonio to uncover his chest.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: But as he was: about to cut Antonio's flesh, Portia stopped him.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: She cried out, " Wait a second, Shylock' Never forget - there is no mention of blood in the bond.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Therefore, you cannot shed a single drop of blood while you cut your pound of flesh; or else you pay the penalty.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: And the penalty is, the state will take your property from you.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: You lose everything that you have now, Shylock."

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Shylock understood it was not possible for him to cut a pound of flesh without shedding blood.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: He was defeated by the wise lawyer.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: He hung his head and without another word left the courtroom.

passages.heading: Lesson 11: the trial
passages.text: Thus Antonio's life was saved.
